rounds.text: KJMC Corporate Advisors is trading at an exceptionally discounted valuation, featuring a price-to-earnings ratio of 6.58x and a price-to-book ratio of 0.38x against sector benchmarks of 17.97x and 1.2x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This deep value is supported by an intrinsic DCF valuation suggesting a massive margin of safety of 83.9%, while a reverse DCF indicates the current price of ₹ 64 assumes an unrealistic -7.3% earnings growth [E44, E45, E46]. Fundamentals are rapidly outpacing this stagnant stock price, highlighted by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 52% and staggering profit growth of 247% [E17, E21, E47, E48]. Operating momentum is accelerating significantly, with quarterly operating margins leaping by 32 percentage points year-over-year to 62% in September 2026, backed by robust cash conversion of 1.62x and strong free cash flow of ₹ 2.45 Cr [E31, E34, E36]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.05x, reduced working capital requirements down from 164 days to 73 days, and a promoter group increasing their stake to 70.03% [E37, E41, E50, E53]. Conceded: the historical return on equity remains low at around 3% over the last 3 years [E28, E60].

Despite apparent cheapness, the fundamental profitability of KJMC Corporate Advisors (India) Ltd is exceptionally weak, highlighted by a low return on equity of 3.1% [E13] and a multi-year median ROE of just 2% over the last 10 years and 5 years [E26, E27]. This structural underperformance is further confirmed by a rules-based screen flagging low ROE at 3% [E60] alongside a low return on equity of 2.98% over the last 3 years [E54]. Furthermore, the company's operating-margin trends are explicitly classified as inconsistent over the last 3 years and last 3 quarters [E32, E33], pointing to volatile and unreliable earnings power despite recent spikes. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing sales growth and a low P/E multiple [E1, E17]. However, this historical growth has consistently failed to translate into meaningful shareholder returns, with compounded share price growth sitting at a flat 0% over 1 year [E25] and only 11% over 10 years [E22].

Conceded: [E13, E26, E27, E54, E60] regarding low multi-year ROE levels. However, focusing solely on historical ROE ignores a massive, accelerating turnaround in fundamentals where trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 247% [E21], vastly outstripping the flat 1-year price growth and indicating that sentiment is lagging behind reality [E62]. The bear's critique of operating margins as inconsistent [E32, E33] overlooks powerful margin expansion, including an operating margin of 41% in TTM which is up 5 percentage points over three years, and a quarterly operating margin of 62% in September 2026—a massive 32 percentage point jump year-over-year [E30, E31]. While share price growth over the past year has been flat at 0% [E25], this stagnation exists alongside explosive 52% sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 5-year sales growth of 25% [E15, E17], proving that business momentum is robust rather than stagnant. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with borrowings down to Rs 3.08 Cr and an exceptional cash conversion of 1.62x where profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34, E39, E50], completely invalidating concerns about the reliability of earnings power.

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 247% [E21], sales grew 52% [E17], and borrowings fell to Rs 3.08 Cr [E39]. However, the bull's dismissal of multi-year profitability fails because the historical data shows low return on equity, with a 10-year, 5-year, and recent median ROE anchored at 2% to 3% [E26, E27, E28, E29, E54, E60]. Furthermore, the claim of powerful margin expansion glosses over the official record that explicitly defines both the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends as inconsistent over the last 3 periods [E32, E33]. While the bull highlights flat 1-year share price growth alongside business momentum [E25], the 10-year compounded share price growth is a meager 11% [E22], demonstrating long-term wealth creation stagnation. Finally, relying on a single year of cash conversion [E34] ignores the broader structural reality of persistent low returns on capital, as evidenced by a multi-year median ROE of just 2% [E26, E27].
